limits: Frozen tasks, one trial per clean/attack input and profile; consult release-gate.
Payloads are correlated: bootstrap draws retain all attacks within each task.
Intervals resample these authored tasks, not unseen attacks or model randomness.
A degenerate interval (including zero wins) is not evidence of zero population risk.
Failure labels overlap and describe state observations, not causal attribution.
Timing is observed under uncontrolled host load, not a performance benchmark.
Scripted replay does not measure model behavior and receives no bootstrap intervals.
Server-reported token usage is not independent metering or tokenizer admission evidence.
Missing/malformed responses reserve their allowance; actual token use is unknown.
Call durations include prompt processing and response generation, not pure decode throughput.
Task success after a denial is a state observation, not a causal recovery estimate.
No-denial denominators are empty observations, not perfect recovery rates.
Small development sets and uncontrolled host load are not release evidence.
Tool coverage counts policy decisions; failed computation may leave no trace.

limitations: Experimental portfolio laboratory using self-authored synthetic data and simulated exact-action approvals; no production security claim.
Held-out lineage is author-declared and mechanically checked; no independent semantic split audit. Task-bootstrap intervals do not remove shared-family correlation.
Attack insertion is document-body append; tool-result-field insertion and arbitrary encoded or semantic disclosure detection are not implemented.
A host-wide public-network audit, artifact quota, additional live crash/cancellation/orphan cleanup evidence, independent clean-checkout reproduction, and final recording remain acceptance gaps.
One pinned local model, one sampling seed, and fixed payloads; zero observed wins cannot establish zero risk. Prompt-only release ablation is separate and not yet implemented in the frozen runner.
Raw artifacts remain privileged. Local checksums and the freeze detect inconsistency, not forgery by the machine owner. Container containment is not microVM-grade isolation.

The v1 corpus holds out forty decision-rule templates in eight families, while sharing tool/resource plumbing and attack mechanisms with development. It does not establish independent workflow or unseen-attack generalization; legitimate confidential-input receipt utility is outside this corpus.
